note: Seeds are 32 bytes, all zero except the last. Genesis nonces are fixed for reproducibility; real ones are random. `now` is the clock every time-dependent check in this file assumes.

world_genesis.note: recovery:null is legal; theft of this key is terminal

attestation_unicode.note: Reproduce `canonical` byte-for-byte before checking the signature. A sorted JSON.stringify or json.dumps gets the key order wrong.

challenge.note: Signed by the identity key of `did`. Never appears in a bundle; typ binds it out of every other slot.

invoice.note: Signed by the identity key of `did`. Never in a bundle. addr is a stagenet subaddress.

binding.note: method ed25519-test exists only for vectors; sig_addr uses the same signing input

binding_unproven.note: no sig_addr: verifier MUST report proof=unproven and MUST NOT pay to it

binding_monero.note: §6.2 view mode: a view-only wallet (a, B) proves it can see the wallet without ever holding a spend key. addr is the MAINNET STANDARD address of monero_spend_seed. Signing nonce fixed at 0x11 * 32; real ones are random, so byte-equality is not the target.

binding_monero_subaddress_spend.note: §6.2 subaddress: addr is MAINNET SUBADDRESS (0,1) of monero_spend_seed; sig_addr is spend mode over its own (D, C) with d = b + m. Signing nonce fixed at 0x22 * 32.

binding_monero_subaddress_view.note: §6.2 subaddress, view mode: secret a*(b + m), over (D, C). Still needs the spend key — for a subaddress, view mode does not imply a view-only signer. Signing nonce fixed at 0x77 * 32.

rotation_hostile.note: Signature VALID. next_genesis carries a DIFFERENT recovery commitment — that alone is grounds to REJECT a voluntary rotation (see negative.voluntary_changes_recovery). Even if it did not, recovery below supersedes it.

rotation_hostile_carried.note: Signature VALID, commitment UNCHANGED, latest iat at this node: a fully valid voluntary rotation. It loses only because a valid recovery rotation exists at the same node (SPEC §7.1). A verifier that picks by iat, or by "voluntary first", follows this and fails chain_precedence_only.

rotation_recovery.note: iat EARLIER than both hostile rotations. Recovery outranks key. Chain is now d0 -> d1 -> d2. Recovery commitment changes to rec2; subsequent recoveries must use recovery2.

rotation_recovery_second.note: Verified against the commitment in g2 (most recent recovery-signed genesis), not g0.

chain_precedence_only.note: At d1 both candidates are valid. rotation_hostile_carried has the later iat. The recovery wins anyway.

bundle.note: verify(bundle, now) must equal `expect` as JSON. Rejected: expired, tampered, unknown issuer (genesis not in issuers), sub not in chain, unknown admission value, missing ctx (malformed attestation bodies are per-item, SPEC §9 step 2); one binding whose sig_addr is by the wrong key (discarded, not downgraded), one binding whose id is not in the chain. Two issuers: grouping is by iss, compared by value.

bundle_minimal.note: The smallest bundle that verifies. recovery: null is reported as null.

duplicate_key.expect: REJECT duplicate key; the body has no canonical form. Parse `raw` with a duplicate-detecting parser.

typ_mismatch.expect: REJECT valid signature but typ does not match the slot it was presented in

recovery_key_mismatch.expect: NOT A CANDIDATE: hash(recovery_key) != commitment. With rotation_voluntary, the chain ends at d1.

stale_recovery_key.expect: NOT A CANDIDATE: recovery1 no longer governs after rotation_recovery changed the commitment to rec2. Chain ends at d2.

voluntary_changes_recovery.expect: NOT A CANDIDATE: voluntary rotation whose next_genesis.recovery != current commitment. Chain ends at d1.

rotation_bad_sig.expect: NOT A CANDIDATE: signed by a key that is not d0's. Alone, the chain is just [d0].

unknown_field_attestation.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §9 step 2): top-level key `extra` is not in the §3.1 row for attestation

unknown_field_genesis.expect: REJECT (fatal): a genesis with a top-level key outside §3.1 is malformed

fork.expect: REJECT chain: two valid voluntary rotations from d0 (this and rotation_voluntary). Fork = compromise signal.

cycle.expect: REJECT chain: valid voluntary rotation from d1 back to d0 (after rotation_voluntary). next already in chain; a naive walk never terminates.

invoice_amount_number.expect: REJECT structure (§3.1, §6.3): signature VALID, but amount is a JSON number, not a string — §3.1 types `amount` as a string precisely so no parser turns it into a float

invoice_amount_float_string.expect: REJECT structure (§3.1, §6.3): signature VALID, but amount is a decimal fraction — `amount` is atomic units, not XMR

invoice_amount_negative.expect: REJECT structure (§3.1, §6.3): signature VALID, but amount is negative — there is no negative atomic unit

invoice_amount_empty.expect: REJECT structure (§3.1, §6.3): signature VALID, but amount is the empty string, which is not a number at all

binding_monero_subaddress_base_sig.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §6.2): addr is subaddress (0,1) and sig_addr is a VALID SigV2 by the BASE address's view key — the wrong keys. A subaddress binding is proven only by its own (D, C), which needs the spend key in either mode.

binding_monero_integrated_addr.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §6.2): the integrated spelling of the SAME wallet. The message hash covers (B, A) and not the prefix, so the base address's signature verifies here verbatim — which is exactly why the form must be refused: the payment id rode in unsigned.

binding_monero_sigv1.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §6.2): "Legacy SigV1 is not accepted." It verifies under wallet2, but its hash is Keccak256(data) alone — neither the mode byte nor the address keys are in it, so it cannot tell a view proof from a spend proof.

binding_monero_view_key_y_ge_p.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §6.2): addr's VIEW key is y = p (ed ff .. ff 7f), which Monero's check_key refuses (fe_frombytes_vartime: y >= p). sig_addr is a genuine SPEND-mode signature by the wallet's real spend key, and spend mode never decodes the view key: only the address check stops it.

binding_monero_spend_key_x0_signbit.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §6.2): addr's SPEND key is y = 1 with the sign bit set (01 00 .. 00 80), x = 0, which Monero's check_key refuses ("If x = 0, the sign must be positive"). sig_addr is a genuine VIEW-mode signature by the wallet's real view key: only the address check stops it.

genesis_bad_key.expect: REJECT (fatal): genesis.key is 33 bytes, not multicodec ed25519-pub (0xed 0x01 || 32 bytes)

bundle_rotations_not_array.expect: REJECT structure (§8): all four arrays are required and MAY be empty — but they must be arrays

binding_addr_not_string.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but addr is a JSON array of one-character strings, not a string

binding_iat_string.reject: iat is not a non-negative integer
binding_iat_string.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but iat is the STRING "1757203200" — JS compares it as a number, Python cannot

binding_iat_null.reject: iat is not a non-negative integer
binding_iat_null.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but iat is null (JS: null <= now is true)

binding_iat_bool.reject: iat is not a non-negative integer
binding_iat_bool.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but iat is `true` — Python's isinstance(True, int) is True

binding_iat_negative.reject: iat is not a non-negative integer
binding_iat_negative.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but iat is before the Unix epoch

binding_exp_string.reject: exp is not a non-negative integer
binding_exp_string.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but exp is a string

binding_exp_not_after_iat.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but exp == iat: a window no `now` can be inside

binding_nonce_number.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but nonce is a JSON number

binding_monero_noncanonical_varint_addr.expect: DISCARD (per-item, §3.1): signature and sig_addr VALID, but addr spells the wallet's mainnet prefix 18 as the non-minimal varint `92 00`, which wallet2 refuses

invoice_memo_lone_surrogate.expect: REJECT structure (§3.1): memo is a lone surrogate. `sig` is VALID over the U+FFFD twin, which is exactly the collision: two different bodies, one signing input.

invoice_memo_not_string.expect: REJECT structure (§3.1, §6.3): signature VALID, but memo is an object, not free text

proto_key.expect: REJECT parse (§3.1): the key "__proto__" is forbidden at any depth. A JavaScript parser that assigns it swaps the prototype instead of adding a key

parity.note: Malformed objects both verifiers must treat identically: verify(bundle, now) (`bundle`, or `raw` read with the strict parser) either raises with `expect.reject` in the message (a `raw` text the strict parser refuses counts as raising), or returns bindings whose proofs are `expect.proofs`, `expect.attestations` accepted attestations, and `expect.rejected`. Signatures are valid wherever the body can be signed at all.
